title: Spending and capacity

predict.q: Start: demand for goods = 460, productive capacity = 500, so there is spare capacity. Output = 460; price level = 100. Demand rises by 80, and capacity does not change. What happens to output and the price level?

options.s: Output rises to 540; the price level stays at 100
options.fb: Output cannot go above capacity. Only 40 of the extra 80 can be produced; the rest pushes up prices.

options.s: Output rises to 500; the price level rises to 120
options.fb: The first 40 of extra demand uses up the spare capacity; the other 40 has nowhere to go but higher prices.

options.s: Output rises to 540; the price level rises to 120
options.fb: Output is capped at capacity, 500. Firms cannot make goods with workers and machines they do not have.

options.s: Output stays at 460; the price level rises to 140
options.fb: There was spare capacity of 40, so output does rise, to 500. Only the extra demand beyond that raises prices.

task: Move the demand slider and the capacity slider and watch output and the price level.

target.do: Move the demand slider to +80 (capacity +0), then press Check.

takeaway: Extra spending raises output only while there is spare capacity. After that, it mostly pushes up prices. Lasting growth needs capacity to grow too.
